key_insight: Among three detonation-sprayed WC coatings, WC–Co–Cr offered the best overall combination of hardness, friction, scratch resistance, and corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: WC–Co–Cr coatings could extend the service life of pipeline valves and other oil-and-gas components exposed to wear and corrosion.
method: Deposited WC coatings with Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binders by detonation spraying.
Characterized microstructure and composition using SEM and EDS mapping.
Evaluated microhardness, tribology, scratch resistance, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: WC–Co–Cr achieved 1232.55 HV and a friction coefficient of 0.515, while porosity ranged from 0.40% for WC–Ni to 2.78% for WC–NiCr; corrosion testing used 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
watch_item: Laboratory results do not establish long-term durability under combined wear and corrosion in operating valves.
paper_title: Impact Of Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binder systems on the microstructure and functional properties of WC coatings produced by detonation spraying
